note: PLAT-007 validate Windows filesystem: the test does both halves the case asks for - supported cases work, unsafe cases fail explicitly - and records what this machine actually did rather than what documentation promises. Measured on the host: a non-ASCII name (café-日本語-δ.txt) round-trips byte for byte; a path far beyond the historical MAX_PATH was accepted by the product's own policy but the platform stopped after 18 components, an explicit and recorded refusal rather than a half-built tree; creating a reparse point was refused with PermissionDenied (no developer mode on this machine), which is an explicit answer; and deleting a *running* executable failed with AccessDenied - the locked-executable case the case names. That last one replaced a first attempt that opened a file and deleted it: Windows allows that because the handle is opened with share-delete, so the test now starts a copy of the program and deletes it while it runs, which is the lock that matters. Fault proof: making the portable path policy refuse paths its own limit allows fails the policy assertion (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain. Recorded on the host platform.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
